Theorem 1.1.title: Theorem 1.1 · Goldbach asymptotics under Hypothesis S
Theorem 1.1.summary:
Fix a nonzero smooth compactly supported weight \(\phi\). Suppose every sufficiently large even integer satisfies GRH and Hypothesis S holds for the chosen admissible \(h\). The error constant depends only on \(\phi\); the threshold may also depend on \(h\).
\[|G(N)-c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)|\le C_\phi\mathfrak S(N)/h(N),\qquad G(N)\sim c_\phi\mathfrak S(N).\]

Theorem 1.2.title: Theorem 1.2 · Error bound under Hypothesis R
Theorem 1.2.summary:
Suppose all sufficiently large even integers satisfy \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\) and Hypothesis R. The error constant depends only on \(\phi\). The supplementary result establishes \(R\Rightarrow S(h)\) for each admissible \(h\) fixed in advance.
\[|G(N)-c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)|\ll_\phi\sqrt{\mathfrak S(N)/N}(\log N)^{3/2}.\]

Lemma 3.1.title: Lemma 3.1 · Finite projection onto odd characters
Lemma 3.1.summary:
For even \(N\ge4\) and a nonzero smooth compactly supported weight, the finite character projection gives the correlation identity and the nonnegative projection bound below.
\[G(N)=D(N)-P(N),\qquad 0\le P(N)\le D(N)\ll_\phi\log N.\]

Proposition 3.2.title: Proposition 3.2 · Analytic structure and positivity of the character kernel
Proposition 3.2.summary:
Fix even \(N\ge4\). The double series converges absolutely for \(\Re s,\Re z>1/2\). The kernel is jointly meromorphic on \(\mathbb C^2\), with possible poles from the logarithmic derivatives. Under GRH it is jointly holomorphic for \(\Re s,\Re z>0\). The conjugated kernel is Hermitian positive semidefinite, and its section space is finite dimensional with dimension at most \(\varphi(N)/2\).
\[P_N(s,z)=\sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(nm,N)=1}}\frac{\Lambda(n)\Lambda(m)}{n^{1/2+s}m^{1/2+z}}\left(\mathbf1_{n\equiv m\pmod N}-\mathbf1_{n\equiv-m\pmod N}\right).\]
\[P_N(s,z)=P_N(z,s),\qquad\overline{P_N(s,z)}=P_N(\bar s,\bar z).\]

Lemma 3.3.title: Lemma 3.3 · Paired zero expansion of the completed L-function
Lemma 3.3.summary:
The nontrivial zeros of a primitive odd character are counted with multiplicity. At points where both completed L-values are nonzero, the difference of logarithmic derivatives has the absolutely and locally uniformly convergent expansion below. The number of zeros with \(t\le\Im\rho<t+1\) is \(O(\log(d_\chi(|t|+2)))\), uniformly in conductor, character, and height.
\[\frac{\mathcal L'}{\mathcal L}(u)-\frac{\mathcal L'}{\mathcal L}(u_0)=\sum_\rho\left(\frac1{u-\rho}-\frac1{u_0-\rho}\right).\]

Lemma 3.4.title: Lemma 3.4 · Logarithmic derivative expansion and growth under GRH
Lemma 3.4.summary:
Under \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), the zero-difference series \(Z_\chi(s)\) converges absolutely and locally uniformly for \(\Re s>0\), with multiplicities retained. On each fixed compact interval \(I\subset(0,\infty)\), the logarithmic derivative is \(O_I(\log^2(N(|t|+2)))\), uniformly in \(N,\chi,t\).
\[g_\chi(s)=Z_\chi(s)+\frac{L'}L(2,\chi)-\frac12\left(\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma(\tfrac34+\tfrac s2)-\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma(\tfrac32)\right)+e_\chi(\tfrac12+s)-e_\chi(2).\]

Lemma 3.5.title: Lemma 3.5 · Double Mellin representation of the second moment
Lemma 3.5.summary:
Fix even \(N\ge4\) and an admissible weight. The two vertical integrals are independent and absolutely convergent for \(\sigma>1/2\). Under GRH the identity extends to \(0<\sigma\le1/9\). The off-diagonal congruences split into \(m=n+kN\), \(n=m+kN\), and \(n+m=kN\), with signs \(+,+,-\). When both weights are nonzero, the first two families vanish and the last has only \(k=1\).
\[P(N)=\frac1{(2\pi i)^2}\int_{(\sigma)}\int_{(\sigma)}N^{s+z}\widetilde\Phi(s)\widetilde\Phi(z)P_N(s,z)\,ds\,dz.\]

Lemma 4.1.title: Lemma 4.1 · Beta integrals for the three continuous models
Lemma 4.1.summary:
Write \(w=s+z\). Assume \(h>0\), \(\Re s,\Re z<1/2\), and \(\Re w>0\). All three integrals below converge absolutely. Their signed sum is \(h^{-w}K_-(s,z)\); for \(h=kN\), the common local density gives the full model \(\mathfrak S(h)h^{-w}K_-\).
\[\int_0^\infty x^{-1/2-s}(x+h)^{-1/2-z}\,dx=h^{-w}B(\tfrac12-s,w),\]
\[\int_0^\infty x^{-1/2-z}(x+h)^{-1/2-s}\,dx=h^{-w}B(\tfrac12-z,w),\]
\[\int_0^h x^{-1/2-s}(h-x)^{-1/2-z}\,dx=h^{-w}B(\tfrac12-s,\tfrac12-z).\]

Lemma 4.2.title: Lemma 4.2 · Factorization of the signed Beta kernel
Lemma 4.2.summary:
For \(\Re s=\Re z=\sigma\) with \(0<\sigma\le1/9\), the first formula bounds the kernel. The factorization is a global meromorphic identity, represented by a common quotient of entire functions.
\[|K_-(s,z)|\le2B(\tfrac12-\sigma,2\sigma)+B(\tfrac12-\sigma,\tfrac12-\sigma).\]
\[K_-(s,z)=2^{1-w}\Gamma(w)\cos(\pi w/2)X_1(s)X_1(z),\qquad w=s+z.\]

Lemma 4.3.title: Lemma 4.3 · Diagonal and singular-density series
Lemma 4.3.summary:
Fix even \(N\ge4\). The diagonal series converges absolutely and is holomorphic for \(\Re w>0\). The density series converges absolutely for \(\Re w>1\); its continuation is meromorphic for \(\Re w>0\), with the single simple pole and residue below. The Euler product converges normally in this half-plane. For each fixed strip \(0<\sigma_-<\sigma_+\) and \(|\Im w|\ge1\), the continuation is bounded by \(C(N/\varphi(N))(1+|\Im w|)\), and \(N/\varphi(N)\le C\log\log N\).
\[\lim_{w\to1}(w-1)\mathfrak S_N(w)=\frac N{\varphi(N)}.\]
\[1<\mathfrak S(N),\qquad C_2\frac N{\varphi(N)}\le\mathfrak S(N)\le\frac N{\varphi(N)}.\]
\[\mathfrak S_N(w)=\mathfrak S(N)\zeta(w)\prod_{\substack{p>2\\p\nmid N}}\left(1+\frac{p^{-w}}{p-2}\right).\]

Proposition 4.4.title: Proposition 4.4 · Holomorphic continuation of the Beta model
Proposition 4.4.summary: For even \(N\ge4\), the original Beta model equals `continuedModel` pointwise on `betaDomain`. The continued model is jointly holomorphic on the paper's two-variable domain \(\Omega\), encoded by `analyticDomain`.

Proposition 4.5.title: Proposition 4.5 · Holomorphic and Hermitian arithmetic residual
Proposition 4.5.summary: For even \(N\ge4\) satisfying \(\operatorname{GRH}(N)\), the residual \(E_N(s,z)\) is jointly holomorphic on \(\Omega\), symmetric under exchange and conjugation, and \(E_N(s,\overline z)\) is Hermitian.

Proposition 5.1.title: Proposition 5.1 · Weighted kernel and analytic differential identities
Proposition 5.1.summary:
Standing assumptions: \(N\) is even, \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\), \(\beta=1/8\), and \(\sigma_*=1/9\). Under the standing assumptions below, \(E_N(s,\bar z)\) and \(\kappa_N(s,z)=E_N(s,\bar z)/((1+s)(1+\bar z))\) are Hermitian and holomorphic in \(s,\bar z\). The weighted kernel extends to a neighborhood of the closed strip. The differential identity and the exact strip gaps are:
\[(\partial_{\bar s}+j\partial_z)E_N(s,\bar z)=0,\qquad \sigma_*-\alpha_N>1/90,\quad\beta-\sigma_*=1/72.\]

Lemma 5.2.title: Lemma 5.2 · Fourier–Laplace realization of the Hardy space
Lemma 5.2.summary:
For arbitrary \(\alpha<\beta\), the Fourier–Laplace transform is a unitary map from the weighted \(L^2\) space to the strip Hardy space. Both boundary traces exist in \(L^2\), and their joint image is closed. The inner product is linear in its first argument, as in the paper.
\[U\psi(s)=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(\tau)e^{s\tau}\,d\tau,\qquad w_H=e^{2\alpha\tau}+e^{2\beta\tau}.\]
\[\|U\psi\|_{H^2}^2=\|h_\alpha\|_2^2+\|h_\beta\|_2^2=\int_{\mathbb R}|\psi(\tau)|^2w_H(\tau)\,d\tau.\]

Proposition 5.3.title: Proposition 5.3 · Compact spectral structure of the residual operator
Proposition 5.3.summary:
Standing assumptions: \(N\) is even, \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\), \(\beta=1/8\), and \(\sigma_*=1/9\). The weighted boundary kernel belongs to \(L^2(\Gamma_N\times\Gamma_N)\). Its operator \(T_N\) is compact, self-adjoint, and Hilbert–Schmidt. Nonzero eigenvalues are counted with multiplicity. The operator norm equals \(\sup_j|\mu_j(N)|\), attained when \(T_N\ne0\).
\[\sum_j\mu_j(N)^2=\|T_N\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2=\iint_{\Gamma_N^2}\frac{|E_N(s,\bar z)|^2}{|1+s|^2|1+\bar z|^2}\,|ds|\,|dz|.\]

Proposition 5.4.title: Proposition 5.4 · Reproducing kernel and pointwise estimates
Proposition 5.4.summary:
Standing assumptions: \(N\) is even, \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\), \(\beta=1/8\), and \(\sigma_*=1/9\). Let \(\Delta_N=\beta-\alpha_N\) and \(d_N(s)=\min(\Re s-\alpha_N,\beta-\Re s)\). The formulas give the reproducing kernel, its exact norm, and the induced residual estimate. On \(\Re s=\sigma_*\), the residual is bounded by an absolute constant times \(\|T_N\|(1+|v|+|t|)^2\).
\[k_z(s)=\frac1{4\Delta_N}\csc\frac{\pi(s+\bar z-2\alpha_N)}{2\Delta_N},\qquad h(s)=\langle h,k_s\rangle.\]
\[\|k_s\|^2=\frac1{4\Delta_N\sin(\pi(\Re s-\alpha_N)/\Delta_N)}\le\frac1{8d_N(s)}.\]
\[|E_N(s,\bar z)|\le\frac{\|T_N\||1+s||1+z|}{8\sqrt{d_N(s)d_N(z)}}.\]

Proposition 6.1.title: Proposition 6.1 · Existence and intrinsic entirety of the spectral product
Proposition 6.1.summary:
Standing assumptions: \(N\) is even, \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\), \(\beta=1/8\), and \(\sigma_*=1/9\). The quaternionic spectral product converges locally uniformly, is independent of enumeration, and defines an intrinsic entire slice-regular function. The trace and determinant identities below hold; the determinant identity is on the usual complex slice.
\[X_N(q)=\prod_j\left(1-\frac{4\mu_j(N)^2}{\delta_N^2}q(1-q)\right)\]
\[\operatorname{tr}(T_N^2)=\sum_j\mu_j(N)^2=\|T_N\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2.\]
\[X_N(q)=\det\left(I-\frac4{\delta_N^2}q(1-q)T_N^2\right).\]

Proposition 6.2.title: Proposition 6.2 · Symmetries and critical-plane values
Proposition 6.2.summary:
Standing assumptions: \(N\) is even, \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\), \(\beta=1/8\), and \(\sigma_*=1/9\). The spectral function satisfies \(X_N(0)=X_N(1)=1\), \(X_N(1-q)=X_N(q)\), and \(X_N(\bar q)=\overline{X_N(q)}\). The centered and critical-plane products are below. The latter is real and independent of the unit imaginary quaternion \(I\). For real \(x\notin(0,1)\), \(X_N(x)\ge1\).
\[X_N(1/2+\xi)=\prod_j\left(1-\frac{\mu_j^2}{\delta_N^2}+\frac{4\mu_j^2}{\delta_N^2}\xi^2\right).\]
\[X_N(1/2+It)=\prod_j\left(1-\frac{\mu_j^2}{\delta_N^2}(1+4t^2)\right)\in\mathbb R,\]

Proposition 6.3.title: Proposition 6.3 · Zero spheres, real zero pairs, and multiplicities
Proposition 6.3.summary:
Standing assumptions: \(N\) is even, \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\), \(\beta=1/8\), and \(\sigma_*=1/9\). For each nonzero eigenvalue put \(d_j=\delta_N^2/\mu_j(N)^2\). The three cases below classify all zeros. There are finitely many exceptional real pairs, and every real zero lies in \((0,1)\). Nonreal zero spheres are invariant under unit-quaternion conjugation. Reflection and conjugation preserve slice multiplicities; the central order is even.
\[\begin{cases}
\Re q=1/2,\quad|\Im q|=\sqrt{d_j-1}/2,&d_j>1,\\
q=1/2\text{ (double factor root)},&d_j=1,\\
q=1/2\pm\sqrt{1-d_j}/2,&0<d_j<1.
\end{cases}\]

Theorem 6.1.title: Theorem 6.1 · Exact equivalence of zero-free regions and operator norms
Theorem 6.1.summary:
Standing assumptions: \(N\) is even, \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\), \(\beta=1/8\), and \(\sigma_*=1/9\). The pointwise spectral condition \(\mathcal R(N)\) is equivalent to \(\|T_N\|\le\delta_N\). For \(0<\eta<1/2\), the zero-free half-space has the exact norm criterion below. A bound \(\|T_N\|\le M_N\), with \(M_N>\delta_N\), gives the displayed width. When this width is at most \(1/4\), it is comparable to \(\delta_N^2/M_N^2\).
\[X_N(q)\ne0\ (\Re q>1-\eta)\iff\|T_N\|\le\frac{\delta_N}{2\sqrt{\eta(1-\eta)}}.\]
\[\eta(M_N)=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-\delta_N^2/M_N^2}}2\in(0,1/2)\]

Theorem 6.2.title: Theorem 6.2 · Baseline zero-free region from GRH
Theorem 6.2.summary:
Absolute constants and an absolute threshold give the Hilbert–Schmidt bound below for all sufficiently large even \(N\) satisfying \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), together with the stated baseline zero-free width.
\[\|T_N\|\le\|T_N\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\ll(\log N)^2.\]
\[\eta_N^{\mathrm{GRH}}\asymp\frac{\mathfrak S(N)}{N\log N},\qquad
X_N(q)\ne0\quad(\Re q>1-\eta_N^{\mathrm{GRH}}).\]

Lemma 6.4.title: Lemma 6.4 · Mean energy bound for logarithmic derivatives
Lemma 6.4.summary:
Standing assumptions: \(N\) is even, \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\), \(\beta=1/8\), and \(\sigma_*=1/9\). For \(0<\sigma\le\beta\), average over all odd characters, including imprimitive characters. The implied constant in the estimate below is independent of \(N,\sigma\).
\[\frac2{\varphi(N)}\sum_{\chi\in X_N^-}\int_{\mathbb R}
\frac{|g_\chi(\sigma+it)|^2}{1+t^2}\,dt
\ll(\log N)^2+\sigma^{-2}.\]

Proposition 6.5.title: Proposition 6.5 · Trace and norm bounds for three operator components
Proposition 6.5.summary:
Assume even \(N>e^{10}\), \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), and \(\alpha_N=1/\log N\). The arithmetic and diagonal operators are positive trace class; the model operator is Hilbert–Schmidt. A single absolute \(C>0\), independent of \(N\) and \(\alpha_N\), gives the three bounds below. The local names `P`, `D`, and `K` refer to these operators.
\[\|\mathcal P_N\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\operatorname{tr}\mathcal P_N\le C\bigl((\log N)^2+\alpha_N^{-2}\bigr),\]
\[\|\mathcal D_N\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\operatorname{tr}\mathcal D_N\le C\alpha_N^{-2},\]
\[\|\mathcal K_N\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le C\alpha_N^{-2}.\]

Lemma 7.1.title: Lemma 7.1 · Mellin inversion and decay of the weight
Lemma 7.1.summary:
For an admissible weight \(\phi\), let \(\Phi(u)=\sqrt u\,\phi(u)\). Mellin inversion holds for every real \(\sigma\) and \(u>0\). On each fixed vertical strip, the transform has uniform decay \(C(1+|\Im s|)^{-6}\). If even \(N\ge4\) satisfies GRH, the character integral holds for every odd \(\chi\) and \(0<\sigma\le1/9\). The inversion, character integral, and double second-moment integral are absolutely convergent.
\[P_\chi=-\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(\sigma)}N^s\widetilde\Phi(s)g_\chi(s)\,ds.\]
\[\Phi(u)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(\sigma)}\widetilde\Phi(s)u^{-s}\,ds\qquad(u>0).\]

Lemma 7.2.title: Lemma 7.2 · Inversion of diagonal and model terms
Lemma 7.2.summary:
Fix even \(N\ge4\), an admissible weight, and \(0<\sigma\le1/9\). The diagonal double Mellin integral equals \(D(N)\), while the density and signed Beta-kernel integral equals \(-c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)\). Both are absolutely integrable. The companion declarations establish convolution integrability, equivalence of half-line and finite-interval formulas, and \(J_0(1)=c_\phi\).
\[\frac1{(2\pi i)^2}\iint_{(\sigma)^2}N^{s+z}\widetilde\Phi(s)\widetilde\Phi(z)D_N(s+z)\,ds\,dz=D(N),\]
\[\frac1{(2\pi i)^2}\iint_{(\sigma)^2}\widetilde\Phi(s)\widetilde\Phi(z)\mathfrak S_N(s+z)K_-(s,z)\,ds\,dz=-c_\phi\mathfrak S(N).\]

Proposition 7.3.title: Proposition 7.3 · Arithmetic meaning of the residual double integral
Proposition 7.3.summary:
For even \(N\ge4\) satisfying GRH, an admissible weight, and \(0<\sigma\le1/9\), the double Mellin integral involving \(N^{s+z}\), the two weight transforms, and \(E_N(s,z)\) equals the quantity below. The corresponding two-variable real integral is absolutely integrable.
\[c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)-G(N).\]

Proposition 7.4.title: Proposition 7.4 · Riesz vector and exact norm of the weight functional
Proposition 7.4.summary:
For an admissible weight and even \(N>e^{10}\), every interior vertical line defines the same continuous functional \(\ell_N\) and Riesz vector \(v_N\). Put \(V(u)=\Phi(u)-u\Phi'(u)\). The exact norm and upper bound are below. In addition, \(Q_N=e^2\mathcal E_\phi+O_\phi(1/\log N)\), where \(\mathcal E_\phi=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^\infty|V(u)|^2du/u\).
\[Q_N=\|\ell_N\|^2=\|v_N\|^2=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty\frac{(Nu)^{2\alpha_N}|V(u)|^2}{1+(Nu)^{-2\Delta_N}}\,\frac{du}{u}\le e^2\mathcal E_\phi.\]

Theorem 7.1.title: Theorem 7.1 · Operator quadratic form for the Goldbach error
Theorem 7.1.summary:
For even \(N>e^{10}\) satisfying GRH, an admissible weight, and the standard Hardy realization, the arithmetic residual is exactly the operator quadratic form below. The supplementary bound has a constant depending only on the weight.
\[c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)-G(N)=\langle T_Nv,v\rangle,\qquad |c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)-G(N)|\le Q_N\|T_N\|.\]
\[|c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)-G(N)|\le e^2\mathcal E_\phi\|T_N\|,\]

Lemma 7.5.title: Lemma 7.5 · From zero-free width to relative arithmetic error
Lemma 7.5.summary:
For each admissible weight there is \(C>0\), chosen before \(N,\eta\), such that the bound below holds for even \(N>e^{10}\) satisfying GRH whenever \(0<\eta\le1/4\) and the spectral function has no zeros in \(\Re q>1-\eta\). Along such even integers, divergence of the displayed ratio implies \(G(N)/(c_\phi\mathfrak S(N))\to1\).
\[\frac{|G(N)-c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)|}{c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)}\le C\sqrt{\frac{(\log N)^3}{N\eta\mathfrak S(N)}}.\]
\[\frac{N\eta_N\mathfrak S(N)}{(\log N)^3}\longrightarrow\infty,\]

Proposition A.1.title: Proposition A.1 · Realization with left boundary c/log N
Proposition A.1.summary:
Fix an admissible weight and \(c>0\). For even \(N\ge4\), \(N>e^{10c}\), and GRH, put \(\alpha_{N,c}=c/\log N\). The boundary kernel defines a compact self-adjoint Hilbert–Schmidt operator and satisfies the corresponding pointwise estimate. The strip gaps, functional norm, and arithmetic pairing are below. The asymptotics fix \(c\) first; the pairing is independent of \(c\), and \(c=1\) recovers the main text.
\[\alpha_{N,c}<1/10,\quad \Delta_{N,c}>1/40,\quad \sigma_*-\alpha_{N,c}>1/90,\quad\beta-\sigma_*=1/72.\]
\[Q_{N,c}=\|\ell_{N,c}\|^2=\|v_{N,c}\|^2\le e^{2c}\mathcal E_\phi,\qquad Q_{N,c}=e^{2c}\mathcal E_\phi+O_{\phi,c}(1/\log N).\]
\[c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)-G(N)=\langle T_{N,c}v_{N,c},v_{N,c}\rangle,\quad |c_\phi\mathfrak S(N)-G(N)|\le Q_{N,c}\|T_{N,c}\|.\]

Proposition A.2.title: Proposition A.2 · Spectral conditions and asymptotics for fixed c
Proposition A.2.summary:
Fix an admissible weight \(\phi\) and \(c>0\). For even \(N\ge4\), \(N>e^{10c}\), and \(\mathrm{GRH}(N)\), the pointwise spectral condition \(\mathrm R(N,c)\) is equivalent to \(\|T\|\le\delta\). For \(0<\eta<1/2\), zero-freeness in the open half-space \(\Re q>1-\eta\) is equivalent to \(\|T\|\le\delta/(2\sqrt{\eta(1-\eta)})\). Substituting \(\eta_N(h)\) gives the bound below when \(h(N)>0\) and \(0<\eta_N(h)\le1/4\). The GRH baseline bound \(\|T\|\le C(\log N)^2\) and width \(c_0\mathfrak S(N)/(N\log N)\) have constants depending only on \(c\). The arithmetic error constant depends only on \(\phi,c\) and is chosen before \(h\). Under `HypothesisSAt(c,h)` or `HypothesisRAt(c)`, each sufficiently large even integer satisfying GRH has error at most \(C\mathfrak S(N)/h(N)\) or \(C\delta_N\), respectively. The threshold in the S estimate may depend on the growth and admissibility of \(h\).
\[\|T\|\le\frac{\mathfrak S(N)}{2h(N)\sqrt{1-\eta_N(h)}}.\]

Lemma A.3.title: Lemma A.3 · Balancing the functional norm and operator baseline
Lemma A.3.summary:
For each admissible weight there are positive \(L,U\) depending only on the weight and an absolute \(C>0\). The first bounds hold for sufficiently large even \(N\) satisfying GRH and every \(0<a<1/10\). With \(a=c/\log N\), the product \(Q_aM_a\) is comparable to \((\log N)^2e^{2c}(1+c^{-2})\); the balancing factor diverges as \(c\downarrow0\) or \(c\to\infty\). When the exact widths for the target norm \(\mathfrak S(N)/(hQ_a)\) and baseline \(M_a\) both exist and are at most \(1/4\), their ratio is comparable to the final expression below.
\[LN^{2a}\le Q_a\le UN^{2a},\qquad \|T_a\|\le M_a=C\bigl((\log N)^2+a^{-2}\bigr).\]
\[\frac{h^2(\log N)^4}{\mathfrak S(N)^2}e^{4c}(1+c^{-2})^2.\]

Proposition A.4.title: Proposition A.4 · Obstruction to approaching the boundary at fixed modulus
Proposition A.4.summary:
Fix even \(N\ge4\) satisfying GRH and a nontrivial zero \(1/2+i\gamma\) of an odd character. The positive coefficient and lower limit below force \(\|T_{N,c}\|\ge z_N/c\) and failure of R for sufficiently small \(c\). One can choose \(z_N>0\) and \(0<c_N\le\log N/24\); every admissible width \(0<\eta\le1/4\) then satisfies the last bound. Companion statements give the near-zero convergence of \(R_N\) and \(\mathfrak S(N)R_N(0)=1\).
\[C_{N,\gamma}=\frac2{\varphi(N)}\sum_{\chi\in X_N^-}m_\chi(1/2+i\gamma)^2>0.\]
\[\liminf_{c\downarrow0}c\|T_{N,c}\|\ge\frac{2C_{N,\gamma}\log N}{1+\gamma^2}>0.\]
\[\eta\le\frac{\delta_N^2c^2}{3z_N^2}.\]

Proposition B.1.title: Proposition B.1 · Wide-weight counting formula at N = 30030
Proposition B.1.summary:
Fix \(N=30030\), \(A=16\), and \(L=1000\). The cutoff is \(C^6\), symmetric about \(N/2\), and equals one on \([L,N-L]\). With companion weight \(W\), put \(f(u)=W(u)/\sqrt u\). The weight product on its support and the exact counting identity are below.
\[f(u)f(1-u)=\frac{\eta(Nu)^2}{\log(Nu)\log(N(1-u))}.\]
\[r_G(N)=\frac N2\mathcal J-\frac{\mathcal C_{\rm pp}}2+\mathcal E.\]

Lemma B.2.title: Lemma B.2 · Wide-weight character integrals and second moments
Lemma B.2.summary:
At \(N=30030\), every Dirichlet-character counting integral on \(\Re s=1\) is absolutely integrable and satisfies the formula below. The wide-weight correlation is the signed second moment of these exact integrals; the diagonal counting moment is the unsigned second moment. Both use normalization \(\varphi(30030)=5760\).
\[I_\chi=-\sum_{n<N}a_n\chi(n).\]

Lemma B.3.title: Lemma B.3 · Propagation of integral error to the prime-pair count
Lemma B.3.summary:
Given approximations \(\widehat I_\chi\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the displayed mean-square error condition bounds the correlation error by \(2\sqrt{\widehat D}\,\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2\). Multiplication by \(N/2\) gives `countError` for the unordered prime-pair count and the integer enclosure below. The normalization of the main term is \(A=N\mathfrak S(N)c_f/2\).
\[\frac1{5760}\sum_\chi|I_\chi-\widehat I_\chi|^2\le\varepsilon^2,\]
\[r_G(N)\in[\widehat r_G-\varepsilon_r,\widehat r_G+\varepsilon_r]\cap\mathbb Z.\]

Proposition B.4.title: Proposition B.4 · The same operator represents the wide-weight residual
Proposition B.4.summary:
Assume \(\operatorname{GRH}(30030)\). The continuous wide-weight functional is represented by its Riesz vector \(v_W\), and the residual equals the quadratic form below for the main-text residual operator with the standard left boundary. The integral is absolutely convergent; the wide weight is \(C^6\) with compact support in \((0,1)\).
\[\langle T_{30030}v_W,v_W\rangle,\]

Proposition B.5.title: Proposition B.5 · Finite spectral model of order 2562
Proposition B.5.summary:
Assume \(\operatorname{GRH}(30030)\). The complex matrix from 1281 trapezoidal nodes on each boundary has a real eigenvalue list and unitary diagonalization. Its determinant spectral function is the product below, with symmetry \(q\mapsto1-q\). If the matrix operator norm is at most \(\delta\), every complex zero has real part \(1/2\).
\[\prod_j\left(1-\frac{4\lambda_j^2q(1-q)}{\delta^2}\right),\]

ConditionalGoldbach.interiorLine_memLp.title: Supporting result · L² membership of interior Hardy lines
ConditionalGoldbach.interiorLine_memLp.summary:
For \(a<b\), \(a<x<b\), and an element \(\psi\) of the weighted \(L^2\) space, the function below belongs to \(L^2\) for Lebesgue measure on the real line. This supplies the interior-line element of Lean's `Lp` type.
\[t\longmapsto\operatorname{FourierLaplace}(\psi)(x+it)\]

ConditionalGoldbach.boundaryTraces_exist.title: Supporting result · Existence of both L² boundary traces
ConditionalGoldbach.boundaryTraces_exist.summary: For \(a<b\) and \(\psi\) in the Hardy model, two real-line \(L^2\) elements are the limits of the interior-line functions as \(x\) approaches \(a\) and \(b\) from within the strip.

ConditionalGoldbach.primePair_consequenc.title: Supporting result · Prime-pair lower bound in the central interval
ConditionalGoldbach.primePair_consequenc.summary:
Fix an admissible weight. Suppose all sufficiently large even \(N\) satisfy GRH and either `HypothesisR` holds or `HypothesisS(h)` holds for some \(h\). Then there is \(C>0\) such that the displayed central prime-pair lower bound holds for every sufficiently large even integer.
\[\#\left\{p\in\mathbb N:\frac N3\le p\le\frac{2N}3,\ \operatorname{Prime}(p)\land\operatorname{Prime}(N-p)\right\}\ge C\frac{\mathfrak S(N)N}{(\log N)^2}.\]
